name: Bhutan (Thimphu and Paro)
summary: The Land of the Thunder Dragon: dzongs, monasteries, the Tiger's Nest and mountains; tightly regulated, high-quality tourism.
season_note: March-May and September-November have the best weather. Winter is cold; monsoon (June-Aug) is rainy.
entry_note: Bhutan: Bangladeshi passport holders usually need a visa through an authorised tour operator and the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) applies; check the latest rules with the embassy before booking.

reach.how: Dhaka to Paro International Airport (Drukair/Bhutan Airlines; often via Kolkata or Bangkok) (Drukair, Bhutan Airlines)
reach.note: Only Druk Air and Bhutan Airlines fly to Paro; check Dhaka-Paro availability.

reach.how: Dhaka to Phuentsholing via Banglabandha/Siliguri then Thimphu by road
reach.note: Check land-route permissions; most use flights.

attractions.name: Taktsang (Tiger Nest) Monastery
attractions.what: A famous cliffside monastery reached by a 2-3 hour hike.

attractions.name: Tashichho Dzong
attractions.what: The seat of government and monastic body.

attractions.name: Buddha Dordenma
attractions.what: A giant golden Buddha statue overlooking the valley.

attractions.name: Rinpung Dzong and National Museum
attractions.what: A fortress monastery and museum in the old watchtower.

attractions.name: Punakha Dzong
attractions.what: The most beautiful dzong at the river meeting.

rules: Tourism is by guided package; SDF applies.
Dress modestly at dzongs; remove hats and shoes.
Smoking and tobacco sales are heavily restricted.
Do not point feet at Buddha statues.
